question: The transposition of Directive (EU) 2019/1937 in Spain has been arbitrary and incomplete. This means that, legally, reporting channels have to be internal, dependent and subordinate, whereas the directive requires them to be external, independent and autonomous. In addition, the Independent Authority is attached to and appointed by the Ministry of Justice.

It is not external, or independent, or autonomous, or a single authority of Union law pursuant to the European criteria outlined in various CJEU rulings. What is more, government departments and public bodies – in particular those of the central government and the justice department – have not set up their reporting channels.

Finally, no legal procedure has been established to make it possible to enforce the decisions of the few reporting channels that do comply with the directive and that have been recognised in final court decisions, such as Aspertic’s reporting channel.
To make matters worse, the judiciary is not allowing the channels’ decisions to be enforced owing to a lack of jurisdiction and because there are no procedures in place. 1.
What is the Commission planning to do in the face of these compliance failures?
Given that a single European jurisdiction is proposed within the meaning of Article 2 of the directive, can whistleblowers request protection before other channels and courts? Which ones?
answer: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 (1) requires Member States to ensure that legal entities establish channels and procedures for internal reporting and follow-up. Member States shall designate the authorities competent to receive external reports. These channels must be designed in a manner that ensures the completeness, integrity and confidentiality of the information reported.

In order to ensure the enforcement of EU law and to protect reporting persons, it is important that the reports are handled by channels that are established in accordance with the directive: internal channels established by legal entities enabling, at least, their workers to report information on breaches; internal channels provided by a third party entrusted by a legal entity; or external channels operated by competent authorities designated by the Member States.

Within the framework of the directive, it is for the national authorities, including national courts (or for specific European institutions, agencies and bodies, where relevant) to ensure effective follow-up to whistleblower reports and to address any breaches identified. This includes an assessment whether reporting persons qualify for protection under the applicable national legal framework..

In January 2022, the Commission initiated infringement procedures against 24 Member States, including Spain, for failing to transpose the directive by 17 December 2021. In February 2023, Spain notified to the Commission the measures transposing the directive.
The Commission is currently assessing the compliance of these measures and will not hesitate to take further action, as required, in the event of breaches of the directive.
Directive (EU) 2019/1937 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2019 on the protection of persons who report breaches of Union law, OJ L 305, 26/11/2019, p. 17-56.
